newsitem.title: UK: Kazakh central banker doubts Samurai bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh central banker doubts Samurai bond issue.

text.p: Kazakhstan may shelve plans to issue a yen-denominated Samurai bond this summer and opt instead for another dollar Eurobond issue in the second half of the year, its central bank chief said on Monday.

Uraz Jandosov told Reuters that a Samurai bond had been considered as one possibility for the former Soviet republic's second foray into the sovereign debt market but talks with Japanese financiers had been unproductive.

"We talked with various companies, including Japanese investment banks which handle placements of Samurai bonds, but these were not warm discussions," Jandosov said after a presentation at the annual meeting of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD).

In late March, the head of Kazakhstan's National Securities Commission said the oil-producing republic would raise $200-250 million in the summer with a Samurai bond -- a yen-denominated bond issued in Japan by a foreign borrower.

But Jandosov said Kazakhstan's second issue on international bond markets would be in the latter half of the year, probably in dollars. It would be placed after the country's credit rating is raised, he added.
Moody's and Standard and Poors have given Kazakhstan Ba3 and BB- ratings respectively for long-term foreign currency debt.
Jandosov said the next Eurobond issue would be bigger than last December's successful debut placement of $200 million.
